title: At 12:00, the Sun disappears. You won't know for 8 minutes.
sources: Live Science, 'What would happen to Earth if the sun suddenly vanished?' (29 Mar 2026), with Timothy Cronin (MIT) and Michael Summers (George Mason University): https://www.livescience.com/planet-earth/what-would-happen-to-earth-if-the-sun-suddenly-vanished
Business Insider, 'Here's what would happen if the sun disappeared right now': https://www.businessinsider.in/Heres-what-would-happen-if-the-sun-disappeared-right-now/articleshow/48430503.cms
Chris Baird, West Texas A&M, 'What is the speed of gravity?': https://wtamu.edu/~cbaird/sq/mobile/2013/04/30/what-is-the-speed-of-gravity/index.html

shots.text: At noon, the Sun disappears. For 8 minutes and 20 seconds, nobody on Earth will know.
shots.say: At noon, the Sun disappears. For eight minutes and twenty seconds... nobody on Earth will know.

shots.text: You're in the park. Sun on your face. But that light left before the Sun vanished. You're feeling a ghost.
Even gravity hasn't heard. It moves at light speed too. Earth keeps circling an empty spot.
12:08 and 20 seconds. The lights go out.
shots.say: Twelve oh eight, and twenty seconds. The lights go out.

shots.text: No sunset. Just off. The Moon goes black too. It was only ever a mirror.
Gravity lets go. Earth flies off in a straight line, 30 kilometres every second.
shots.say: Gravity lets go. Earth flies off in a straight line, thirty kilometres every second.

shots.text: One bright dot still shines. Jupiter. Its light was already on the way. An hour later, it goes out too.
Then the cold. Scientists estimate around 20 degrees lost per day at first.
shots.say: Then the cold. Scientists estimate around twenty degrees lost per day, at first.

shots.text: In two or three days, it's freezing everywhere. Ponds freeze. Plants sleep, like winter. This winter never ends.
But the oceans don't freeze solid. Ice forms a lid, and underneath, the water could stay liquid for decades.
At the bottom, by volcanic vents, bacteria keep living. They never needed the Sun. They eat Earth's own heat.

label.text: LIFE THAT NEVER NEEDED THE SUN

shots.text: Your move? Copy them. Go underground. Geothermal power. Food under lamps.
And somewhere four light years away, anyone looking at our Sun still sees it shining. For four more years.
If you had 8 minutes of sunlight left, what would you do?
shots.say: If you had eight minutes of sunlight left... what would you do?
